action: Hunt for the published EggStreme indicators retrospectively, watch for unexpected listening ports and new inbound firewall rules on servers, and review DLL sideloading and lateral movement over file shares.
exec: A suspected China-linked espionage toolkit is being rebuilt to avoid beacon-based detection, so networks that rely on outbound traffic alerts may miss it.
plain: Security firm Bitdefender says a spy toolkit it first found in 2025 has been reworked and is still used against several Philippine government bodies, and it now hides better.

key_findings: Bitdefender assesses with high confidence that the operation still targets several Philippine government organisations, and with low to medium confidence Taiwan; victims are not named.
The operators rebuilt the malware after the 2025 report: AES-256-CBC for the Fuel configuration, new loader ciphers, and an agent moved from gRPC to raw TCP with mutual TLS.
New agent builds add Active Directory reconnaissance, proxy and PowerShell commands and drop the keylogger.
Behaviour that stayed constant: DLL sideloading, in-memory execution and lateral movement over shares through a staging host outside endpoint management.
Attribution is unchanged: a suspected Chinese APT.
recommendations: Restrict built-in tools such as WScript, cmd and reg to roles that need them and alert on scripts run from C:\Users\Public.
Inventory unmanaged machines reachable over SMB, monitor SMB-launched scripts and alert on new inbound firewall allow rules.
Enable script block logging and detect in-process PowerShell and CLR loading.
Build detections on the constant behaviours, not hashes, and capture process memory before remediation.

sources.name: Bitdefender Business Insights: EggStreme Malware: Rebuilt Under Scrutiny

summary: Bitdefender updated its EggStreme research on November 18, saying with high confidence that the operation continues to target multiple Philippine government organisations, with Taiwan possible at low to medium confidence. It says newer builds use mutual TLS and include a passive variant that never beacons out. Bitdefender keeps its earlier attribution to a suspected Chinese APT group.
title: Bitdefender: EggStreme backdoor rebuilt to evade detection, still aimed at Philippine government bodies

validation.note: Bitdefender's own post (read via a fetch agent) and GBHackers' coverage agree on the November 18 update, targeting confidence levels and attribution.

review.note: Compared 18 Nov date, high-confidence Philippine government targeting, Taiwan low-to-medium, unchanged suspected Chinese APT, mutual TLS, passive variant, keylogger absence with Bitdefender post and GBHackers
